answer: Because the jade ledger attributes every share, the ember audit publishes the split and self-attestation collapses into a single position. A farm has to staff both sides of that split with keys it controls, thus it pays the nectar fee twice and still divides one payout. Only 45% of a settled reward goes to the author; the rest is split among the identities that attested to it, so authoring alone does not pay. That is 27 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
